notes: Cross-language PARITY suite for the redaction floor. One set of payload -> expected-redaction fixtures, run by
BOTH the TypeScript suite (@flanj/redaction-patterns: SDK + control-plane DLP) and the Go suite (collector
internal/redact). Both must produce these exact results; this file, not either implementation, is the contract.
It complements redaction-vectors.json (scalar/recognizer-level vectors) with structured bodies: nested and
undocumented fields, arrays, PAN-as-number, base64 decode-then-scan, inbound (request) bodies, form-encoded and
truncated bodies, the negatives that must survive, and the poisoned-spec cases for the schema-aware enhancer.
kind=json: `input`/`expected` are JSON VALUES. Each suite asserts BOTH entry points: (a) structural
redact(input) deep-equals `expected` with hits == `patterns`; (b) the text path redactText(serialize(input)),
parsed back, deep-equals `expected` with the same patterns. Deep-equality (not serialized bytes) is the
parity oracle for json cases so JS/Go serializer differences (key order, number formatting) cannot mask or
fake a redaction difference. Numbers/bools/null are left untouched EXCEPT an integer of 13-19 digits that
passes Luhn (PAN-as-number) and a 3-4 digit number under a CVV key, which become string tokens.
kind=text: `input`/`expected` are strings; the text path must match BYTE-FOR-BYTE (the text path rewrites only
the scalars that fired and preserves every other byte, so both languages emit identical bytes).
Every case must also be idempotent: redacting `expected` again yields `expected` with no patterns.
`enhancer` (optional): the schema-aware enhancer is applied to the FLOOR'S OUTPUT with `spec` (a list of
{path,type}; path = dot-separated keys, `[]` = every array element; type = a floor PatternId). `expected` is
the enhanced value and `patterns` the hits the enhancer itself reported. INVARIANT (asserted by both suites
over the cross product of every json case x every spec in this file): the enhancer only ever ADDS tokens -
every token present in the floor output is present, unchanged, at the same path, after enhancement.
Direction is documentary: `inbound` marks request bodies (higher PAN density than responses). The floor applies
identically to every captured body regardless of direction or edge classification.
All card numbers are well-known public test numbers, never real PANs.
`fields` (optional; absent = MUST be empty): the captured-value-property records both implementations must
emit for WHOLE-VALUE redactions — the scalar was replaced by exactly one token. Span-in-text redactions,
redacted object keys, form-encoded pairs and non-JSON text bodies emit no fields (a top-level scalar body
that is wholly redacted uses path "", the RFC 6901 root). Each record: `path` (RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into
the body; `~`->`~0`, `/`->`~1`), `pattern` (the emitted token id) and `props` of the ORIGINAL value:
type (string|number; integer flag for numbers), length in UNICODE CODE POINTS of the original scalar text
(numbers: their literal), containsLowerCase (a-z), containsUpperCase (A-Z), containsDigits (0-9),
containsASCIIControlChars (<=0x1F or 0x7F), containsASCIIPrintableChars (0x20-0x7E),
containsASCIIExtendedChars (>0x7F). Props are NON-REVERSIBLE by design: never add anything that narrows
the value (no prefixes/suffixes, no entropy). Records are sorted by path. For kind=json BOTH entry points
must produce these exact records; for kind=text the text path must. Purpose: drift detection can validate
the decidable constraints (type, min/maxLength) of a redacted field instead of skipping it.

cases.description: Bare 16-digit Luhn-valid PAN as a JSON string value
PAN grouped 4-4-4-4 with spaces; detection on normalized digits, the whole original span is redacted
PAN grouped 4-4-4-4 with dashes
15-digit Amex grouped 4-6-5 (the grouping many naive PAN regexes miss)
14-digit Diners Club PAN (shortest common length above the 13-digit floor)
13-digit Visa PAN (the minimum PAN length)
19-digit Luhn-valid PAN (the maximum PAN length; brand-prefix-gated validators reject it, the Luhn floor must not)
19-digit PAN printed 4-4-4-4-3 (five groups)
Luhn-valid PAN whose prefix (2200, Mir) is absent from common brand tables — the floor is Luhn-gated, never BIN-gated, so it is still redacted
16-digit Maestro PAN
PAN transmitted as a JSON NUMBER, not a string — still redacted (becomes a string token); an integer amount is not
PANs inside a JSON array of strings
PANs inside objects inside an array
The canonical hostile payload: PAN in a documented field AND in an undocumented nested `metadata.backup_card`; non-Luhn order_id, last4 and amount survive; phone in free text is caught
PAN six levels deep, through arrays and objects
PAN used as an object KEY (a map keyed by card number) — keys are scanned too
PAN embedded in a free-text JSON value; only the PAN span is replaced
PAN followed by a space and more digits (e.g. an expiry) — the PAN is still found; the trailing digits survive
A separated digit group BEFORE the PAN (a leftmost-greedy regex tests the wrong 16 digits and leaks the card); the real PAN must be found
PAN as a form-urlencoded value
PAN inside an XML element (non-JSON text body)
PAN inside a URL path (the SDK redacts target/url with the same floor)
JSON body truncated by the capture cap mid-token: still redacted structurally, every other byte preserved verbatim
JSON body truncated INSIDE the PAN's string literal (no closing quote): the partial body is still scanned as text
Pretty-printed JSON keeps its whitespace, key order and untouched scalars byte-for-byte; only the PAN literal is rewritten
Text that starts like JSON but is malformed: the residue bytes are still scanned as text — nothing is skipped
PAN as a JSON number literal in a text body becomes a string token literal
NEGATIVE: a 16-digit id that fails Luhn (order_id) must survive — no over-redaction
NEGATIVE: a 4-digit last4 is never redacted
NEGATIVE: integer amounts and a 13-digit non-Luhn epoch-ms timestamp (number AND string) are untouched
NEGATIVE: booleans, null, empty string/object/array and zero are untouched
NEGATIVE: UUIDs and hex digests have digit runs adjacent to letters; they are never PAN candidates
NEGATIVE: a 20-digit run is above the PAN length ceiling and is not a candidate
NEGATIVE (deliberate anchoring trade-off): a Luhn-valid run glued to letters/underscore inside an identifier is not a PAN candidate; the schema-aware enhancer covers documented PAN fields
NEGATIVE: a national-format number (no +country) cannot be validated without a region and is left alone (a loose phone regex here is what over-redacts ids)
NEGATIVE: +-prefixed but invalid per phone metadata (fictional 555-555-5555) is not redacted — validated, not pattern-matched
NEGATIVE: 3-4 digit numbers outside a cvv/cvc key are not CVVs; a 5-digit value under a cvv key is not a CVV shape
NEGATIVE: a bare 9-digit number is not an SSN (format-anchored ###-##-####)
NEGATIVE: IBAN-shaped string with a failing mod-97 checksum is not redacted
NEGATIVE: ordinary words that happen to be valid base64 are not decoded into false positives
NEGATIVE: a base64 value that decodes to text with no PII is untouched
NEGATIVE: base64 of binary data (a PNG header) decodes to non-text and is never scanned or redacted
NEGATIVE: three dotted segments starting with eyJ whose header does not decode to a JSON object is not a JWT token
NEGATIVE: ordinary text with durations/ports/versions is unchanged

cases.description: Email as a JSON value
Email with +tag and multi-label domain
Email in prose followed by a period; the period is not part of the redacted span
Email wrapped in angle brackets (RFC 5322 display form)
German IBAN, electronic (compact) format
IBAN in print format (groups of four separated by spaces)
IBANs with letters in the BBAN (GB, FR, NL, ES) — mod-97 validated, not PAN-confused
IBAN followed by another word in prose; the following word is not swallowed
US SSN in ###-##-#### format
E.164 phone number, validated against phone metadata
International numbers in common separated formats: spaces, parentheses, dashes, dots
Phone in prose followed by an extension word and more digits; only the number is redacted
Phone directly followed by another separated digit group: trailing groups are trimmed until the number validates; the extra digits survive
CVV is contextual: the value of a cvv/cvc key, whether a string or a number, becomes a string token
CVV key variants: cvv2, cvc2, card_cvc, security_code, CVV (case-insensitive)
CVV in textual key contexts: form-encoded and key: value prose
Secret-key shaped credentials (sk_live / sk_test / pk_live) inside JSON
Bearer JWT: the whole JWT (header validated as a JSON object) is one TOKEN; the email inside its payload never surfaces
Bearer with an opaque token
A base64 field whose decoded content is JSON containing a PAN: the WHOLE encoded value becomes the PAN token
base64url (unpadded, - and _) encoding of JSON with a PAN
base64 of plain prose containing a spaced PAN
base64 whose decoded content holds only an email: whole value becomes the EMAIL token
An entire text body that is base64 of JSON with a PAN
base64 blob as one form value among others
INBOUND request body with high PII density: PAN, CVV, email, phone, SSN, IBAN; amounts, order_id, last4 and the (optional, off-by-default) IP survive
INBOUND batch request: an array of card objects, every PAN caught, every non-PAN scalar kept
INBOUND form-urlencoded request: percent-encoded email (%40) is decoded-then-scanned; cvv is key-aware; untouched pairs keep their original bytes
OUTBOUND-style response: a provider response that correctly tokenized the card (last4 + brand) has nothing to redact
Fired pattern ids are reported in canonical order PAN, EMAIL, IBAN, SSN, PHONE, CVV, TOKEN, IP regardless of position
Re-redacting an already-redacted body is a no-op: tokens are inert, nothing fires
A body holding both an existing token and a raw PAN: the token is preserved verbatim, the raw PAN is redacted (add-only, never double-wrapped)
POISONED SPEC: a spec that declares nothing sensitive cannot remove the floor's PAN token
POISONED SPEC: a spec pointing at the wrong field ADDS a redaction there; the floor's PAN token is untouched
POISONED SPEC: a spec that mislabels the card field as EMAIL cannot rewrite the floor's PAN token (tokens are immutable to the enhancer)
POISONED SPEC: paths that do not exist in the body are ignored
GOOD SPEC: the spec marks a field the floor has no recognizer for (a UK NI number as SSN-class); the enhancer ADDS it above the floor
GOOD SPEC: `[]` addresses every array element; nested path under each element
MCP tools/call ARGUMENTS carrying a PAN (v0.5 Step B: the request body of an MCP tool call goes through the same floor)
MCP CallToolResult with a PAN nested inside structuredContent (the response body of an MCP tool call): deep traversal reaches it; captured props emitted
MCP CallToolResult whose content[] text carries STRINGIFIED JSON with a PAN: the per-scalar engine finds the PAN inside the JSON string; span-in-text, so no field record
MCP tools/call ARGUMENTS carrying a base64-encoded JSON body with a PAN: decode-then-scan turns the whole encoded run into one token
